Plot with an rvis wrapper

Source: R/rvisplot.R
rvisPlot.Rd

Dispatch a chart request to a wrapper function named by combining `plotter` and `type` (for example, `plotter = "amCharts"` and `type = "bar"` calls `amCharts.bar()`). Wrapper functions standardize common data and aesthetic arguments while retaining plotter-specific configuration.

Usage

rvisPlot(type, plotter, ...)

Arguments

type

Character scalar. Exact chart method suffix implemented by the selected wrapper.

plotter

Character scalar. Exact wrapper prefix. The corresponding function must be named `paste0(plotter, ".", type)`.

...

Arguments passed to the selected wrapper, commonly including `obj`, dimension mappings such as `x` and `y`, and a named `config` list.

Value

The chart object returned by the selected wrapper, usually an htmlwidget.

See also

The “Chart type and plotter reference” and “Configuration reference” vignettes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
species <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, FUN = mean)
rvisPlot(
  type = "bar", plotter = "amCharts", obj = species,
  x = "Species", y = "Petal.Length",
  config = list(title = "Mean petal length by species")
)
} # }
